newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccans vote "yes" to constitutional reform.
newsitem.headline: Moroccans vote "yes" to constitutional reform.

text.p: Moroccans voted overwhelmingly for constitutional reform in a referendum on Friday to give the country a powerful new upper house of parliament to strengthen regional representation.

Interior ministry figures early on Saturday showed that 99.56 percent, or 10.16 million people, voted "yes", with 45,324 voting "no". Turnout was 82.95 percent of the 12.3 million electorate. There were 31,639 spoilt votes.
Pro-government and opposition parties had called for a "yes" vote, but many of those casting their ballots gave their reason as loyalty to King Hassan.
"I voted today to respond to King Hassan's appeal," said Khadija al-Idrissi, a 42-year-old housewife, casting her ballot at the Lycee Hassan II in the capital, Rabat.
The changes to the 1992 constitution will lead to the existing 333-seat parliament being dissolved and two assemblies formed.
A new lower house, the Majlis Anuwab (Chamber of Representatives), will be directly elected and the new upper assembly, the Majlis al-Mustasharin (Consultative Chamber), indirectly.
